t.E150c.agn: IARC classifies 4-MEI in Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic to humans) on the basis of animal studies. The Hong Kong Centre for Food Safety states that normal cola consumption is not expected to cause health problems because of 4-MEI.
t.E150c.body: In an old study in rats (1951), about one third of the colour-giving components appeared to be absorbed; no conclusion could be drawn on the absorption of the colourless components.
t.E150c.eff.0.a: No problem expected with normal consumption
t.E150c.eff.0.t: 4-MEI, which may form during production, is in IARC Group 2B on the basis of animal studies; the Hong Kong Centre for Food Safety does not expect health problems with normal cola consumption
t.E150c.eval: The production by-product 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI) is classified by IARC in Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic); it is common in cola and similar carbonated drinks.
t.E150c.prod: Obtained by heat treatment of carbohydrates together with ammonium compounds. Because ammonia compounds are used (class III), a by-product called 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI) may form during production.
t.E150c.summary: A caramel colour obtained by heating sugar with ammonia compounds. It is used in beer, soy sauce and meat sauces.
t.E150c.what: Gives food a colour ranging from light brown to dark brown.
